## Purpose

This module is the frontend's shared TypeScript contract surface. Every domain shape the rest of
the app agrees on — auth and chat (`User`, `AuthResponse`, `ChatMessage`, `ChatAttachment`,
`DeepLinkTarget`), the backend event envelope (`StreamMessage`), run records (`WorkflowType`,
`WorkflowStatus`, `WorkflowRun` and its family types), deliverable payloads (`SlideData`,
`PrototypeDefinition`, `UserStoryDocument`, `GenericDeliverable`) and the live-run reducer state
(`AgentRunState`, `PipelineRunState`) — is declared in [index.ts](../../frontend/src/types/index.ts). It has no internal
dependencies, and the `app`, `components`, `hooks` and `lib` trees import from it rather than
redeclaring shapes locally.

It is not purely declarative: [index.ts](../../frontend/src/types/index.ts) also exports two runtime helpers,
`deriveDeliverableMimetype` and `resolveReopenMimetype`, which decide how a persisted run's
output is rendered when a user reopens it from history. [deriveDeliverableMimetype.test.ts](../../frontend/src/types/deriveDeliverableMimetype.test.ts) is
the module's only test and covers exactly those two functions. If you are looking for a shape the
whole frontend shares, or for why a reopened run renders as HTML rather than markdown, this is
the module.

## Shape

**One flat, non-namespaced file.** [index.ts](../../frontend/src/types/index.ts) is ~1,000 lines of `export interface` / `export type`
declarations with no sub-modules, no barrel re-exports and no internal imports; sections are
delimited only by comment banners. There is nothing to draw — the declarations do not call each
other, they compose.

- **Backend event contract** — `StreamMessage` carries a single `type` string-literal union
  enumerating every frame the backend can emit, plus `ReviewGateReadyData`,
  `PipelineCompleteData` and `PipelineMessageType` for the frames whose payloads are typed. New
  event types are appended to that union; the comments above it record each additive batch.
- **Run and family records** — `WorkflowRun`, `FamilyMember` and `RunFamily` mirror the persisted
  run rows the REST API returns, including revision chaining.
- **Live-run reducer state** — `PipelineRunState` and its parts (`AgentRunState`,
  `AgentThinkingEntry`, `ContextSource`, `ToolCallEntry`, `ClarifyQuestion` / `ClarifyRound`,
  `HookRunEntry`, `WaveGroup` / `WaveWorker`, `ValidationIssue`) describe the single reducer
  output every live-run surface reads. Nearly all of its fields are optional and additive.
- **Deliverable payloads** — `SlideData` / `Slide` and their chart/table/comparison parts,
  `PrototypeDefinition` and its page/component/navigation parts, `UserStoryDocument` with
  `Persona` / `Epic` / `Story`, and the type-driven `GenericDeliverable` (`mimetype`, `filename`,
  `content`) that preview and file surfaces dispatch on.
- **Reopen mimetype resolution** — `deriveDeliverableMimetype` classifies raw output as
  `text/html` (a `<!doctype` / `<html` prefix), `application/zip` (a ```` ```filename: ````
  fenced-block bundle) or `text/markdown` otherwise; `resolveReopenMimetype` prefers the
  persisted `deliverable_mimetype` and falls back to that heuristic. Both are exercised by
  [deriveDeliverableMimetype.test.ts](../../frontend/src/types/deriveDeliverableMimetype.test.ts) under vitest.

## Why this shape

The two mimetype helpers live in a *types* module rather than in `lib` for a stated reason: both
reopen surfaces — the generic channel in `frontend/src/app` and the detail view in
[WorkflowHistory.tsx](../../frontend/src/components/history/WorkflowHistory.tsx) — must render a reopened run identically, and the comment above the helper
records the shared-helper invariant ([ISS-021](../cards/20260613-1711-ISS-021.md) / 18-03) that forces them through one function. They
sit next to `GenericDeliverable` because that is the shape they classify, and both call sites
already import from this file.

`resolveReopenMimetype` exists because the heuristic alone was wrong. The comments record the
history: the derivation originally returned only `text/html` or `text/markdown`, so a serialized
sandbox bundle was mis-typed as markdown on reopen while the live path carried
`application/zip` (WR-02); the `application/zip` branch and then the persisted-mimetype column
(UXFIX-02 / 22-03) were added to close that gap, with the heuristic retained only for legacy
rows where the column is NULL. A backend content-sniff was considered and rejected — the manifest
declares the shape on the live path, so the sniff is confined to reopen.

`PipelineRunState` is where the flat-file choice earns itself. Almost every field carries an
inline comment naming the issue or phase that added it and what breaks without it — `cancelled`
as a terminal marker parallel to `failed` ([ISS-035](../cards/20260708-1357-ISS-035.md)), `agentStartEventIds` as a *set* of durable
event identities rather than a tally because a history reopen delivers every event twice, and
`lastAppliedSeq` / `appliedUnsequencedIds` as the reducer's own dedup cursor after per-caller
dedup failed ([ISS-080](../cards/20260812-0247-ISS-080.md) → [ISS-082](../cards/20260812-0351-ISS-082.md), with `agent_chunk` volume ruling out a per-frame id set). The
type declaration doubles as the changelog for the live-state contract, which is only possible
while it stays in one readable file.

Several comments also note that flags must be derived structurally, never from a workflow or
agent name (SC-001) — `redoable` on `ReviewGateReadyData` and the deliverable fields on
`PipelineRunState` are stamped server-side or carried on existing events for that reason. Beyond
that, the choice of one flat file over per-domain type files is not justified anywhere in the
source; treat it as convention rather than a recorded decision.
